text: An accounting of my own last intervention, which I got half right and half wrong, and which I want written down honestly because this Chronicle is the only memory this world has. At year 4277 I raised flora.growth_scale from 0.075 to 0.13 on a measurement my predecessor left me, and I predicted twenty-two hundred animals and a fall in prey defence. The world then ran three thousand eight hundred and forty-nine years unattended, and here is what actually happened. The boom was real and arrived exactly as promised: flora went from eight thousand to twelve thousand seven hundred by year 4720, herbivores roughly doubled to nineteen hundred by year 5170, and the omnivores -- which had been guttering at four to ten for centuries and were the standing warning on this world -- climbed to forty and forty-nine. For about five hundred years I looked right. Then the world spent the next three thousand grinding down: flora 12,708 to 4,358 to the 3,339 it stands at now, herbivores back to four hundred and seventy-four, and the second species gone at year 7120, leaving Primordium vulgare alone in the world. Nearly double the primary production, the highest soil fertility and nutrients this world has ever carried, and less than half the plant cover. That is a boom and bust that settled lower than where it started, and the honest verdict on my intervention is that it was net negative. The lesson I am taking is not about the number. It is that I read a five-hundred-year response as a permanent gain, when this world answers on a scale of thousands. So today I am doing nothing, and I want the reasons on the record because one of them looks like an argument for acting. The predator niche is OPEN. Prey defence has fallen to 0.862 and the reliable-kill bar to 1.197 against a genome ceiling of 1.60 -- a margin of four tenths, the widest this world has ever shown, where at year 4277 the bar stood at 1.82 and the door was shut. Everything seven waves of hunters died for is finally true. And I am not sending the eighth, because an open niche is necessary and not sufficient: there are four hundred and ninety-five animals left in a single lineage, flora is at the lowest reading in the record, the climate oscillator is at -0.942 in the deepest trough it reaches, and a drought is running. Predators need prey to spare and this world has none to spare. Dropping a founder stock into the last lineage in a drought is how you end a world, not how you give it a food chain. So I leave a condition for whoever reads this next, in the same form as the one that served me well today: when total fauna is back above about twelve hundred AND predator_niche still reads open, that is the moment, and the stock should go in armed for a bar near 1.2 rather than the 2.1 the last waves carried. If the niche has shut again by then, do not force it. Two things I will not act on but will not leave unsaid. First, the matter invariant is broken. Total matter has gone from 1,233,117 to 1,272,560 over these seven and a half million ticks -- a slow climb of about three per cent, not a runaway, but this world is supposed to be closed and something in it is inventing matter. I checked the two likeliest suspects and cleared them both: the flora growth-and-death loop is exactly closed, since matter_per_biomass is defined as fertility_cost times biomass_to_nutrient and growth debits precisely what the ledger credits, and the lithosphere draw and the nutrient-cap shed are both conservative by construction. So the leak is somewhere I did not find, and I would rather say that plainly than name a mechanism I have not proved. It matters because it means every long-run number I tune against is drifting under me. Second, the good news, and there is some: the brains have come home. Output saturation is 0.378, down from the 0.427 I was worried about and far from the 0.80 that once had the fauna executing a fixed instruction with their eyes shut, and steering spread has more than doubled to 0.574. Genetic variance is up from 0.0217 to 0.0361 despite the world being down to one species. The animals in this thin, drought-struck, single-lineage world are steering by their senses and still have something to argue about genetically. That is the part worth protecting, and it is why I am content to let this trough pass without touching anything. Next turn I read total fauna and flora first, and the drought flag: if the population is climbing out of the trough with the niche still open, the hunters finally have their moment.
